metadata.note: Lewiston/Auburn's second historic rail connection, distinct from the Grand Trunk international main line (see grand_trunk_railway_montreal_portland.geojson): the Androscoggin and Kennebec Railroad, chartered 1847, which built Waterville-Danville Junction (at Auburn, adjoining Lewiston) by 1849-1850. At Danville Junction the A&K connected with the Atlantic and St. Lawrence Railroad (opened 1853, sold to Grand Trunk) for onward travel to Portland -- initially an interchange rather than A&K's own track. The A&K merged with the Penobscot and Kennebec Railroad on Oct 28 1862 to form the Maine Central Railroad, which over subsequent decades built out its own independent Lewiston-Portland trackage (the 'Lower Road'). Maine Central passenger rail service, including this line, ended systemwide in September 1960 -- the same round of cuts that truncated the Bar Harbor Express to Boston-Bangor only that year (see bar_harbor_express.geojson); by 1954 Maine Central was already substituting buses for some Lewiston-Portland trips. Geometry was re-traced from OpenStreetMap on 2026-08-24 and now follows the real alignment through Lewiston and Danville Junction; it still does not distinguish which years used the A&K's own rail from the years of Grand Trunk interchange trackage over the Danville Junction-Portland stretch.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap route relation https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/8968105 ("Waterville Subdivision"), pulled via the OSM API and chained by shared node ids, then clipped to Waterville, Danville Junction and Portland. Supersedes the original town-centroid straight-line chords (2 and 3 points).
metadata.geometry_retrace: 2026-08-24: both features in this file were bare straight-line chords between town centroids -- 2 points for the A&K and 3 for the Maine Central, covering 73 miles without touching any track. Re-traced from OSM to 878 and 1381 points. The traced lengths, 53.9 and 83.3 miles, come out close to the documented ~55 and ~84, which the chords understated by 11 and 14 miles.

properties.speed_source: estimated: late 1840s-early 1860s early steam-era rail; unsourced
properties.geometry_quality: 878 points, 53.9 mi against a documented Waterville-Danville Junction distance of about 55 miles (the old chord measured 43.2 mi). Station snaps: 475 m at Waterville, 1.9 km at Danville Junction; passes Lewiston at 308 m. Drawn to Danville Junction rather than into Lewiston centre because that is where the A&K actually ended and met the Atlantic and St. Lawrence. Traced 2026-08-24 from OpenStreetMap route relation 8968105 ("Waterville Subdivision", today's CSX line over the old Maine Central route through Lewiston), members chained by shared node ids and the chain clipped to the terminals. This REPLACES a straight-line chord between town centroids -- the previous geometry for this corridor was 3 points for the whole 73 miles and did not follow any track. Density is now about 97 m per vertex. No straight-line approximation remains; the longest single tangent between consecutive OSM nodes is 1.40 km.
